claim.claim-text: 1. A method of forming and utilizing a pattern of radiation spots, comprising: forming a desired pattern of spots on a display screen of a processor, breaking up the desired pattern of spots into at least first and second component patterns of spots that individually include respective first and second numbers of less than all of a set number of spots equally spaced around circles having a common center and respective first and second diameters that are different from one another, and thereafter directing radiation according to at least said first and second component patterns of spots in time succession onto a surface of biological tissue.

2. The method of claim 1, wherein forming the desired pattern of radiation spots includes forming an elliptical pattern of said radiation spots, and wherein said first component pattern of spots provides spots along opposing long sides of the ellipse and said second component pattern of spots provides spots along opposing short sides of the ellipse, said second diameter being greater than said first diameter.

3. The method of claim 1 , wherein forming the desired pattern of radiation spots includes forming an elliptical pattern of said radiation spots, and wherein said first component pattern of spots provides spots along opposing long sides of the ellipse, said second component pattern of spots provides a pair of spots along the opposing long sides of the ellipse, and a third component pattern of spots having less than all of the set number of spots equally spaced around another circle having the common center provides a pair of spots along the opposing short sides of the ellipse, a third diameter of the third component pattern of spots being greater than said second diameter.

4. The method of claim 1 , wherein forming the desired pattern includes positioning at least two spots on opposite sides of said center on a line passing through said center, and wherein said first component pattern of spots provides a first pair of said at least two spots on opposite sides of said center and
said second component pattern of spots provides a second pair of said at least two spots on opposite sides of said center.

5. The method of claim 1, wherein forming the desired pattern includes positioning at least two spots on opposite sides of said center on each of at least first and second lines that pass through said center and form an acute angle with each other, and wherein said first component pattern of spots provides a first pair of said at least two spots on opposite sides of said center on each of said first and second lines and said second component pattern of spots provides a second pair of said at least two spots on opposite sides of said center on each of said first and second lines.
6. The method of any one of claims 1-5, wherein the set number of spots is four or more.
7. The method of claim 6, wherein the set number of spots is exactly eight.

8. The method of any one of claims 1-5, wherein directing radiation onto a surface of biological tissue includes exposing a surface of an eye's cornea to at least said first and second component patterns of spots in time succession with a level of energy that shrinks collagen tissue within the cornea with a pattern according to said desired pattern of spots in a manner to reshape the cornea surface.

9. A method of reshaping a surface of a cornea by shrinking collagen tissue therein in regions thereacross according to a pattern of radiation directed onto the surface, comprising: displaying on an instrument screen a background pattern representing areas of the surface of a patient's cornea to be treated, designing a radiation pattern with which the surface of patient's cornea is to be exposed by overlaying the radiation pattern on the background pattern, and exposing the surface of the patient's cornea to radiation to shrink collagen tissue therein according to the designed radiation pattern thereacross.
10. The method of claim 9, wherein the background pattern includes a picture of the patient's eye to be treated.
11. The method of claim 10, wherein the picture includes topographic map of the patient's eye prior to treatment.
12. The method of claim 9, wherein a topographic map of the patient's eye prior to treatment is displayed adjacent the instrument screen while the exposure radiation pattern is being designed.

13. The method of any one of claims 9-12, wherein the designed radiation pattern is formed of at least two exposures to different patterns of a plurality of radiation spots arranged around at least a portion of a circumference of a circle, wherein diameters of the circles of the spot patterns of said at least two exposures are unequal.
14. The method of claim 13, wherein the designed radiation pattern includes an ellipse.

15. The method of claim 13, wherein the method additionally comprises displaying on the instrument screen numerical data of each of said at least two exposures in an order in which the exposures are to be made, said data including for individual exposures at least a diameter of the circle of the pattern of spots, an angle of rotation of the radiation spots around the circle and an identification of those of a fixed number of spots that are present.

16. A method of correcting for astigmatism through reshaping of a surface of a cornea, comprising: designing a pattern of radiation including an elliptical shape to correct for the astigmatism, and exposing the surface of the cornea to said pattern of radiation in a manner to cause collagen tissue within the cornea to shrink according to the elliptically shaped radiation pattern.
17. The method of claim 16 wherein the pattern of radiation includes a plurality of radiation spots spaced apart from one another in an elliptical pattern.
18. The method of claim 17, wherein exposing the surface of the cornea includes exposing the surface to at least two patterns of radiation spots arranged around circles having different diameters.
